tags: why do dogs kick when you rub their belly
script: You rub your dog's belly and one back leg starts kicking like it has a mind of its own, that's not your dog trying to be funny, it's a reflex they genuinely can't control. It's called the scratch reflex, certain spots on a dog's belly connect straight to nerve endings wired to the spinal cord, bypassing the brain entirely, similar to when a doctor taps your knee. Your dog isn't choosing to kick, their body is just automatically responding, trying to get rid of what it thinks might be an itch or a bug. The fact that they let you touch that spot at all still means something though, the belly covers vital organs, so exposing it is a real sign of trust. So the kicking leg is pure reflex, but the belly-up trust behind it is completely genuine. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
